record.original_question: For a typical geodesic gamma(t) in D_mu^s(M), where typical means that the exceptional set of initial velocities has infinite codimension, can one show that the absolute complexity grows linearly, with C(gamma(t)) comparable to t?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold (possibly with boundary), and let $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the group of Sobolev class $H^s$ volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ (with $s > \dim M/2 + 1$), equipped with the right-invariant $L^2$ metric whose geodesic equation is the incompressible Euler equation. For $\eta \in \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$, define the absolute complexity $C(\eta)$ to be the infimum, over all representations of $\eta$ as a composition $\eta = \eta_k \circ \cdots \circ \eta_1$ with each $\eta_i$ lying on a one-parameter subgroup (a shear-type generator), of the total $H^s$-cost of such a factorization (i.e., the minimal number/size of factors needed to represent $\eta$).

Consider a geodesic $\gamma(t)$ in $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ starting at the identity. Call the geodesic "typical" if its initial velocity lies outside an exceptional set of infinite codimension in the tangent space $T_{\mathrm{id}}\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ (the space of divergence-free $H^s$ vector fields on $M$).

Prove that for a typical geodesic $\gamma(t)$ in $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$, the absolute complexity grows linearly in time: that is, $C(\gamma(t)) \asymp t$ as $t \to \infty$ (there exist constants $c_1, c_2 > 0$ depending on $\gamma$ such that $c_1 t \le C(\gamma(t)) \le c_2 t$ for all $t$ sufficiently large).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed in a 2022/2023 survey of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics as a conjecture about linear complexity growth along typical geodesics on the volumorphism group. No subsequent work appears to resolve it; the survey lists it among unresolved problems.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems (arXiv)
status_evidence.snippet: A collection of open problems along with several new constructions in fluid dynamics and a concise survey of recent developments and achievements in geometric hydrodynamics.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as an open problem in this 2022 collection of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics.
